body:
## Summary

Concurrent `scpp build --build-runtime` runs currently appear able to race while rebuilding the same shared reusable runtime artifact.

During OpenM3 verification on `scpp 0.1.46`, multiple isolated repro projects were built in parallel with `--build-runtime`. Several of them targeted the same runtime artifact path:

```text
/home/alexv/__AI/simple_cpp/stable/.prism/runtime/7fa7d1c8608158e6/libruntime.so
```

One run failed during the runtime shared-library link step with a linker crash, while an immediate rerun of the same repro succeeded.

That strongly suggests the problem is not the source feature under test, but concurrent rebuild of the same shared runtime artifact.

## Repro shape

Use two tiny strict projects that share the same runtime profile. For example, these minimal projects are sufficient:

Project A `main.phs`
```php
namespace om3\tools\vector_unset_repro;

$items vector<string> = ["a", "b", "c"];
unset($items[1]);
echo "count=", count($items), "\n";
```

Project B `main.phs`
```php
namespace om3\tools\hash_unset_repro;

$items hash<int> = [];
$items["a"] = 10;
$items["b"] = 20;
unset($items["a"]);
echo "has_a=", isset($items["a"]) ? "yes" : "no", "\n";
echo "has_b=", isset($items["b"]) ? "yes" : "no", "\n";
```

Each project uses an ordinary strict `prism.json` with the same runtime profile.

## Parallel command pattern

Run both at the same time from separate shells:

```bash
cd tools/vector_unset_repro && scpp build --build-runtime
```

```bash
cd tools/hash_unset_repro && scpp build --build-runtime
```

## Observed result

One run can fail while linking the shared runtime artifact, for example:

```text
LINK ../../../../../../simple_cpp/stable/.prism/runtime/7fa7d1c8608158e6/libruntime.so
collect2: fatal error: ld terminated with signal 11 [Segmentation fault], core dumped
```

The exact same project then succeeds immediately on rerun, which points away from a source-level compile problem.

## Expected result

Concurrent `--build-runtime` calls targeting the same shared runtime artifact should not race.

Suggested behavior:

1. `scpp build --build-runtime`
   - rebuild only if the reusable runtime is missing or stale
   - if another process is already rebuilding the same runtime artifact, wait for it or reuse its result instead of launching a competing write/link

2. `scpp build --build-runtime --force`
   - force rebuild intent should still be respected
   - but concurrent writers to the same runtime artifact should still be serialized or guarded by a lock

## Why this matters

OpenM3 often runs multiple small isolated repro builds in parallel while verifying toolchain behavior. Shared-runtime rebuilds should be safe under that workflow.

Right now, parallel `--build-runtime` appears to create avoidable nondeterministic failures around the shared runtime output itself.

## Environment

- `scpp 0.1.46`
- strict Prism++ projects
- shared runtime artifact under the installed SimpleC++ checkout

comments.body:
This still looks like a legitimate open issue.

The report points at a shared-runtime rebuild race rather than a source-level language bug, and the suggested direction makes sense: serialize or guard concurrent writers targeting the same reusable runtime artifact, while still respecting `--force` semantics.

I’m leaving this open for implementation triage. The latest hotfixes did not address runtime-build locking yet.

Fixed in `v0.1.49`.

What changed:
- reusable runtime builds are now serialized with a per-artifact lock
- runtime object/library outputs are published through temp-file + atomic rename instead of writing/linking directly to the final shared artifact path
- project `scpp build --build-runtime` now prebuilds the shared reusable runtime first, then emits the project-local Ninja graph in runtime-reuse mode instead of having each project Ninja graph rebuild the same shared runtime artifact itself

Why this addresses the race:
- concurrent `--build-runtime` calls targeting the same reusable runtime artifact now wait on the same lock instead of competing to compile/link the same output path
- the final shared runtime artifact is only published once a complete build result exists

Validation:
- focused tool tests passed after the change
- parallel smoke repro with two tiny strict projects running `scpp build --build-runtime` at the same time completed successfully on this branch

Released as part of [v0.1.49](https://github.com/alexstanciu-1/simplecpp/releases/tag/v0.1.49).

Fresh evidence from the `0.1.51` OpenM3 pass still points to the same shared-runtime artifact race.

While rerunning two separate tools in parallel with:

```bash
scpp build --build-runtime --build-dependencies
```

one process failed while linking the shared runtime with:

```text
mold: fatal: ../../../../../../simple_cpp/stable/.prism/runtime/16e7359b8887d667/runtime.o: unknown file type
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

The other process completed, and an immediate rerun of the failed command then succeeded.

So the symptom changed compared with the earlier segfault report, but it still looks like the same underlying issue: concurrent writers/readers against the same shared runtime artifact path can leave one process observing a transient invalid runtime object state.

The fresh `0.1.51` report makes this look open again.

The earlier `v0.1.49` work clearly moved the design in the right direction, but the new `mold: ... runtime.o: unknown file type` symptom still points at one process observing a transient invalid shared-runtime artifact state during concurrent `--build-runtime --build-dependencies` activity.

So my current read is:

- the issue should stay open
- this now looks less like a missing-lock problem in the abstract and more like an incomplete serialization/publication boundary somewhere in the reusable runtime build path
- the new repro is especially useful because it shows the failure still exists on `0.1.51`, after the earlier locking/publish changes

The most likely places to inspect next are:

1. whether every shared runtime object/library write path is still protected by the same per-artifact lock
2. whether `--build-dependencies` introduces a second path that can observe or publish runtime artifacts outside that lock discipline
3. whether `runtime.o` or related intermediate outputs are still being written in-place at any step that another process can race against
4. whether the project-local build graph can start consuming a shared runtime artifact before the publishing process has fully completed

So I would keep this open as a real concurrency bug / regression signal rather than closing it as already handled by `v0.1.49`.

I dug into the current implementation and found a concrete regression path in the `0.1.51` tree.

What the earlier `v0.1.49` fix did:

- `scpp build --build-runtime` prebuilt the shared reusable runtime first
- then emitted the project-local `build.ninja` in runtime-reuse mode
- the reusable runtime build helper used a per-artifact `flock(...)`
- runtime object/library publication went through temp-file + atomic rename

What the current `0.1.51` tree was doing instead:

- `execute_build(...)` was still rendering `build.ninja` with `compile_runtime = true`
- that meant the project-local Ninja graph still contained shared-runtime compile/link edges
- `scpp_build_runtime_from_config(...)` had also lost the earlier lock + temp-publish path and was compiling/linking directly to the shared `runtime.o` / `libruntime.so`

That matches the fresh symptom very well: concurrent `--build-runtime` calls could still race on the shared runtime artifact path, including intermediate `runtime.o` visibility.

I restored the earlier safe shape locally:

- prebuild the reusable runtime when `compile_runtime` is requested
- render the project-local Ninja graph in runtime-reuse mode after that prebuild
- restore the per-artifact `flock(...)`
- restore temp object / temp artifact publish + atomic rename

Focused validation after the restore:

- tool tests passed for the build/reuse path
- a targeted check confirmed that a `--build-runtime` build now emits `build.ninja` without `rule compile_runtime` / `rule link_runtime_shared`
- the shared runtime artifact is still produced correctly
- a small parallel smoke repro with two tiny strict projects running `--build-runtime` concurrently completed successfully

So this issue still looks real, and the current root cause appears to be a regression away from the `v0.1.49` safer runtime-build flow rather than just a vague remaining lock bug.

Rechecked on `scpp 0.1.55` (`dbadb86018c4`). The release notes explicitly call out the concurrent shared-runtime rebuild hardening, and a fresh local parallel sanity check with two tiny strict projects running `scpp build --build-runtime --build-dependencies` completed cleanly without the earlier shared-runtime artifact failure shape. Closing as fixed.

title: Important: concurrent scpp build --build-runtime runs should not race on the same shared runtime artifact
